title: Before you arrive
points: You do not need to be an expert, dress perfectly, or know Arabic to enter a masjid. Everyone was new once.
Wear modest, loose, clean clothing that covers the shoulders and knees. For prayer you will kneel and prostrate, so avoid tight clothes.
If you can, try to arrive a little before a prayer time rather than during — it is calmer and easier to follow along.
It is completely fine to just visit and observe your first time without praying.

title: Shoes
points: You remove your shoes before stepping onto the carpeted prayer area. There are shelves or racks near the entrance.
Carry your shoes in or place them on the rack. Many people put them heel-out so they are easy to slip back on.
Socks are fine and normal. You do not pray barefoot as a requirement.

title: Washing (wudu)
points: Most masjids have a washing area to make wudu (the ablution before prayer). Signs usually point to it.
If you have already made wudu at home and not broken it, you do not need to repeat it.
If you are unsure how, it is okay — you can watch others or ask, and you can still sit and observe without praying.

title: Where to stand and how to follow
points: Prayers are in straight rows, shoulder to shoulder, facing the same direction (the qibla). Simply join the nearest row and fill gaps.
Follow the person leading (the imam): when they bow, you bow; when they prostrate, you prostrate. You are not expected to lead anything.
If you don't yet know the words, stay in the posture quietly and say what you know. Nobody is watching to judge you.

title: For sisters
points: Most masjids have a separate area or entrance for women — look for signs, or ask; there is often a sisters' coordinator.
Bring a scarf to cover the hair inside the prayer area. If you forget, many masjids keep spares.
The sisters' section is usually a warm place to ask questions — many reverts find their first friends there.

title: If the prayer has already started
points: Don't worry — quietly join the row and follow along from wherever the congregation is.
You do not need to make up what you missed while inside the group at that moment; just continue with everyone.
If it feels overwhelming, it is perfectly fine to sit at the side and wait until the prayer finishes.

title: What to say to people
points: A warm greeting is 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you). The reply is 'Wa alaykum as-salam'.
It is completely okay to say, 'I'm new, this is one of my first times — can you help me?' People generally respond with kindness.
You are allowed to ask 'dumb' questions. Asking is a sign of sincerity, not ignorance.

title: It's okay to be new
points: Feeling nervous at the door is one of the most common reasons people never go in — you are not alone in that fear.
Cultural cliques can make a masjid feel unwelcoming; if one place feels cold, try another. Warmth exists, keep looking.
The masjid is the house of Allah and it is yours as much as anyone's. You belong there.
